# Surface\-normal gradient schemes

The full gradient of a property QQQ at a face can can be
[interpolated](../interpolation.md) from the
[cell\-based gradient](../gradient/index.md).
The surface\-normal contribution is then represented by:

∇f⊥Q\=n ∙ (∇Q)f \\snGrad Q
 \= \\vec{n} \\dprod \\left( \\grad Q \\right)\_f∇f⊥​Q\=n∙(∇Q)f​
where n\\vec{n}n is the face unit normal. The stencil
for the gradient calculation at the face, fff, between
cells P and N is described by the following figure:
![Surface-normal gradient schematic](data:image/png;base64,)
where the vector d\\vec{d}d joins the two cell centres.
A variety of schemes are available that differ in their
application based on the angle, θ\\thetaθ, between the d\\vec{d}d
and n\\vec{n}n vectors, representing the degree of
non\-orthogonality.

## Usage

Surface\-normal gradient schemes are specified in the
[fvSchemes](../../../../../fundamentals/case-structure/fvschemes.md)file under the `snGradSchemes`
sub\-dictionary using the syntax:

```
snGradSchemes
{
    default         none;
    snGrad(Q)       <snGrad scheme>;
}

```
